text: Testing plays a vital role in creating reliable software. Developers use unit tests to check small, individual parts of the code, such as a single function. In contrast, integration tests verify that different parts of the system work together correctly, catching problems that unit tests might miss. Many teams practice test-driven development, where they write a failing test first and then write code to pass it. This approach encourages cleaner design and prevents bugs early. Ultimately, a strong testing strategy gives developers confidence to make changes, refactor, or add features without fear of breaking existing functionality.
